Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 3)
Topic: Who Is Your God? — Satguru, Param Tattva & the Power of Belief
(Mool Tattva session held on Karwa Chauth day)
Source: Bhaiya's satsang session (video transcript, ~1hr 26min), part of the Mool Tattva series. Purpose: Chatbot knowledge — English version.
1. ON KARWA CHAUTH, FASTS & TRADITIONS

The session opened with a light-hearted discussion of Karwa Chauth (it was Karwa Chauth day). Bhaiya joked about how the fast is practiced in reality — sar gi is eﬀectively a "brunch" wher e anything goes, tea is drunk freely all day ("tea has milk, not water!"), fruits are allowed, and only water is truly given up from evening till moonrise. He repeatedly clariﬁed: "I am not calling anyone wrong — I am only enjoying (anand le raha hoon); I have no intention of hurting anyone's faith."
The serious teachings inside the humor:

Never break your traditions or go against society. "If you go against society, society will not leave you anywhere." Bhaiya will never tell Ashaeiynn members to break their parampara. Follow the norms, maintain the chain — but you should KNOW the truth behind what you do. "You should know that" — awar eness, not rebellion, is the goal. Next time you do anything, you will know what to do and how. The fast does increase aﬀection and love between husband and wife — dr essing up, gifts, photos, togetherness — and that is genuinely good. But the claim that this one-day fast increases the husband's lifespan is completely wrong (sarasar galat). You may grow love through it; you cannot justify pativrata dharma through one ritual day. Logic given: the Mata who originally began this vrat did not fast for just one day. Ganesh Bhagwan is never pleased by a single day's fast — think how long she must have practiced before the deva appeared before her. Real tapasya is continuous, not annual.
2. ON THE "DUPLICACY" OF FAMOUS PREACHERS

Bhaiya gave a pointed commentary (his own words, spoken as "the truth I must tell") on celebrity sainthood, using the currently booming Vrindavan preacher (Premanand Ji Maharaj, whose reels went viral after celebrities like Virat Kohli visited) as the example.

The preacher's famous statement: "One who does not serve his parents is never accepted by God; parents are greater than God; if parents are displeased your downfall is certain; my Kanhaiya and Shri Ji never stay with such a person." Bhaiya's analysis: "Authentically (in principle) this statement is true. Practically it is false." The duplicacy: that same saint left his home and his mother at age 21 and went to the Ganga ghats, then Vrindavan, and did not see his family for ~25 years. "So where were the parents when he was doing bhagwan-bhakti for 25 years? If serving parents is everything, why did he leave them? Either Shri Ji is false, or the parents-claim is false, or your statement is false." Why do saints say such things? "To walk with society, one has to speak this way." They speak from fear of social norms, not from spiritual accuracy. "Don't fall for the smooth, buttery words (chikni-chupdi baatein)." The deeper resolution Bhaiya taught: First awaken yourself; only then can you uplift (taar) your parents. "Only those parents' feet are truly worshipable which have already been washed in Bhagwan's charanamrit." If your parents never received that bhakti, then a son's duty is to attain bhakti himself and, through that bhakti, perform his parents' uddhar (upliftment). But ﬁrst, bhakti of Bhagwan must be done.

Even parents' love ﬂows thr ough God's kripa: "Your parents will love you only when Raghunath Ji's kripa is upon you." Note for the chatbot: present this as Bhaiya's commentary on a principle (celebrity preachers simplify truths for social acceptance), not as an invitation to disrespect any saint. Bhaiya himself says "prava chan sunna achhi baat hai" — listening to discourses is good — his warning is against blind faith in socially-convenient statements.
3. GOD'S KRIPA DECIDES RELATIONSHIPS
One of the emotional cores of this session:

If Bhagwan's kripa is on you: your mother stays with you, your father's hand stays on your head, siblings remain yours even from afar — and even strangers will stand by you as brothers and do what a blood-brother could not. If Bhagwan's kripa is not on you: even your own become strangers. "A birth mother can renounce you saying — what have you ever done for me?" No human being is inherently bad. Without Bhagwan's kripa-tarang (grace-wave), a person becomes bad on their own. The same mother who loved you deeply may one day see everything except you — the change is not her; it is the absence of kripa. Therefore the instruction: "Maa ko mat manao — Bhagwan k o manao." (Don't spend yourself appeasing your mother — appease Bhagwan/Sark ar; the relationships follow.) Beautiful example: a young man said "My mother loves me so much — if I cough at night she brings ginger and puts it in my mouth. My mother's kripa is great on me." Bhaiya corrected him: "You got it wrong, brother. It is Bhagwan's kripa on you that you received such a mother." Kripa is always upstream of the relationship. "Apne to keval Ram — R am hi apne hain." (In the end, only Ram is truly one's own.)
The dark side Bhaiya has personally seen (why divya drishti matters)

Sitting in Ashaeiynn, Bhaiya has seen: a mother-in-law performing tantrik kriya on her daughterin-law; siblings doing tantrik kriya on each other; parents themselves taking their children's tattva to a tantrik to have kriya done on their own children. "The world is not the way it has been shown to you." When divya drishti opens, you begin to see the world's reality. Case: a ~30-year-old man came trembling; Bhaiya saw the man's deceased father seated inside his body. When the pitru was moved aside, the trembling stopped; when it returned, the trembling resumed. Worldly healers say "we'll do healing, we have lama-fera techniques, we'll channel reiki" — but they cannot even see who is sitting inside. "Blind men set out to cure others' pain."
4. WHO IS YOUR GOD? — THE CENTRAL TEACHING
When Bhaiya asked the sangat "Who is Bhagwan?", answers scattered everywhere: Ram Ji, Kul Devta, Isht, Hanuman Ji, the niraakar (formless), atma-so-paramatma, Mahadev, Guru... proving his point:

"You don't even know who YOUR Bhagwan is. If you discover who your Bhagwan is, half your problems end. People spend half their lives searching" — worshipping Krishna, then Hanuman Ji, then Bholenath, then everyone — wandering. First conclusion the sangat agreed on: a human being cannot be it — "insaan out." Nothing rests on humans.
The deﬁnition (from Gurudev — Bhaiya insists the words are his Guru's, in which there is never an error; any error would be his own understanding)

"Bhagwan is that shakti which stands with you in every situation, guides you, consoles you, works for you while you work for it. You do for that shakti, and that shakti does for you. How do we know? Our works keep happening — that shakti is Bhagwan for you."
"There is no greater deﬁnition of Bhagwan than this. Everything beyond this is drama (dramebaazi)."
The three-level alignment
Many shaktis fall under "Bhagwan," but they arrange in three levels:

Level 1 — Y our First God (the shakti behind you / instinct): - Behind every human stands one shakti, present from birth, which keeps the person connected to praan urja (life-energy). - People name it diﬀer ently — "I have Bholenath's shakti," "Hanuman Ji's shakti," "a past-life shakti" — but some shakti always stands behind you. - The moder n world calls it instinct / gut feeling ("I believe in my instinct" — everyone in Hollywood says it). "Just felt lik e it" — that feeling is the ﬁrst step of the energy that pulls you. - It is this shakti/instinct that brought you to Ashaeiynn, that stops you here, that nags you: "The meeting link came — join it. Sit for 5 minutes. Your hand hurts, your leg hurts, work is pending — still, sit a while." "Try to work on your instinct." - This is the ﬁrst ansh of the devata — "atma so paramatma" — the ﬁrst energy of your atma tattva. That is your First God. - Note: this is NOT the kundalini — k undalini shakti must be awakened through dhyaan-yog; it doesn't operate by default.

Level 2 — Satguru (the connector): - The energy that joins your personal shakti to a divine energy is your Satguru — "sarvatra Bhagwan" for you. - Your Satguru: Shri Gurudev Shri Hanuman Ji Maharaj. - When your personal shakti joins a tremendous (jabardast) shakti, that
person becomes unbeatable — both your pulling power and giving power increase. You can draw anything from there, with that shakti standing in between.

Level 3 — P aram Tattva (the supreme element): - Above these stand the Param Tattvas — "woh hamare Ram hain" (some call him Shyam, Ghanshyam, Sitaram, Murari, Tripurari). Mahadev also belongs to the Param Tattva. - The Param Tattva has an order: FIRST come your Kul Devta (family deities), and only after them your Isht. Do not treat your Kul Devta as "small deities of a small temple" — that dismissiveness is a mistak e. - Without a Satguru you cannot connect to the Param Tattva. And without the Param Tattva you cannot manifest anything. - To reach even your Kul Devta, you must ﬁrst get free of the pitrs (ancestral spirits) and take the Guru's sharan — otherwise your puja never r eaches the Kul Devta. Exception: if your pitrs are good, your puja is passed through — but by Gurudev's telling, only about 10 out of 100 pitrs are good (and Bhaiya can see instantly which ones are). Who gives the drishti to see that? The Satguru.
The payoﬀ of alignment
"The one who attains the alignment of all three — the ﬁrst shakti, the Satguru, and the Param Tattva — needs nothing more in this world. He will sit and manifest, and it will happen."
5. WHY A HUMAN GURU CANNOT BE YOUR SATGURU

"If you make a human body your Satguru, you will get thenga (nothing) in the name of gyaan, and in the name of shakti only Bhagwan's naam." Guru-paramparas do carry真 power: "Guru's disciples DO advance — if the parampara is true, they always advance. But they will never advance in gyaan-vigyaan-paravigyaan (knowledge, science, para-science). That is guaranteed." A disciple given Ramayandiksha will sing Ramayan all his life — beautifully, sustained by guru-taap — but no new vidya. Multiple kinds of shaktis can never come from one human body. Example: take diksha from the greatest bhakti-saint — you will r eceive bhakti and a mantra. But can he remove a pret from a body? No — because no one in his parampara ever lear ned that vidya. "Take diksha from any guru in Vrindavan-Mathura, and remove a pret with that mantra — I'll accept it."
The medical-shop man (case study)
A man came to Bhaiya: he had taken guru-diksha from four diﬀerent gurus in Mathura , and chanted one mantra all day at his medical shop — "R adhe Krishna, Radhe Krishna" — for

years. What Bhaiya saw behind him: all four guru-paramparas, four generations deep, standing in lines behind him, with heaps of siddhis visible on his right side. And yet — the man had no money to eat, and a pret in his body: his pitrs sitting crowned on a throne inside him, feeding like kings on all his mantra-energy, while he shriveled. Not one of those gurus or siddhis knew how to remove a pret. "The gurus of his gurus' gurus stood behind him — and not one had the vidya." Bhaiya asked the pitrs to give the boy something; they refused ("we won't let him die" — i.e., they'd keep him alive as their feeder). Then — "one danda (staﬀ-blow) of my Gurudev" — and it was resolved. The vidya to remove pitrs — and to seize the dimensions, dev-shaktis, and authorities standing behind them — comes ONL Y from a Satguru. "Sattguru ke paas har wo gyaan hai jo tumhe chahiye" — a Satguru has every knowledge you need, fr om havanpaddhati to any vidya. (Bhaiya: "I have never learned anything from anyone; my Gurudev taught me everything — he even e xplained M-theory/string theory to me in 15 minutes.") On siddhis: "Siddhis are loyal to no one — they abandon one person and attach to another. That is the world's truth." The world is not as good as it looks.
Hanuman Ji as Guru is not granted cheaply

Ask a human "be my guru" and he'll say "OK." Ask Hanuman Ji Maharaj "please be my Guru" and he will say — "chal, hawa aane de" (go on, let the air pass — i.e., not so fast!). Why? Because the Guru's dayitva (responsibility) is the greatest responsibility in this world. People treat guru-hood as a joke — gr ow a long beard, become a baba, collect footmassages. If you have four siddhis, that does not give you the standing to be a Guru. ("If it does — give me the siddhi of ﬂight, give me a sadhna that r emoves any pret or tantrik. You can't.") Gurudev does not quickly take anyone into his sharan. The reason lies in Surya Vigyan — watch the Mool T attva videos to understand why you came to Ashaeiynn at all. "Until Gurudev sits upon your guru-sthaan, you are only an ASPIRANT." Once the Guru takes the seat — everything is attained ("dhan payo"). How to know you've been accepted, and the vidhi of attaining the Satguru — pr omised for a coming Mool Tattva session.
6. "LET x = a" — THE MATHEMATICS OF FAITH
Bhaiya's signature analogy of this session:

Every math problem says "Find x," and we begin by writing "Let x = a." By ASSUMING a value, the equation resolves — and at the end, the TRUE value of x emer ges. "Maan lene se sachchai saamne aa jaati hai" — by believing, the truth reveals itself .

"The person who believes (maanta hai, vishwas karta hai) — before him Bhagwan manifests, and it becomes true." But faith must hold till the end: if in the middle of the equation you start doubting your own assumption — "x = a was just something I assumed, it's false!" — the entire equation collapses instantly. You'll never ﬁnd x. And if you keep switching assumptions on others' advice ("I solved it with x = 1!" … "tak e x = 2, it comes out ﬁrst-class!") — your vishwas cracks, and no gyaan can help you anymor e. Doubting your own x = a burns everything down ("bhasm ho jaoge"). Application: your entire spiritual shakti is built on your "x = a" — your held belief . Guard it.
Why some knowledge is withheld — the universe question

Knowledge (gyaan) can shake your foundation and your very existence. Story: someone once asked Bhaiya "how was the universe made?" Bhaiya asked Gurudev that evening. As Gurudev began answering, Bhaiya himself stopped him mid-answer: "Baba, no further. If I hear the rest, my faith in you will shake — and if my faith in you shak es, my foundation shakes. I don't want my foundation to shake." Once, Bhaiya taught just one-fourth of what Gurudev had shown him, in a single session. That very day, attacks began on ~90% of the people sitting there — because Gurudev stepped back one step. People took 2–3 months to recover; the topic was never taught again — because people lost faith in their own shakti. Standing instruction: "Never ask me how the universe was made." Some knowledge costs more than it gives.
Gyaan needs Bhakti

"However much gyaan a person has — if the bhakti tattva is not in him, he will never ﬁnd Bhagwan." "Take as much gyaan from me as you want — ﬁll yourself . But as you leave, take bhakti with you." At the Mahotsav, Gurudev distributes bhakti with both hands — "the whole year r emains for distributing gyaan."
7. THE BHAAV CYCLE (Emotion → God)

The veil of Maya (maya ka parda) can only be removed through your subconscious mind, and the subconscious is triggered by emotion (bhaav). One whose bhaav is pure has a direct connection — this is why bhajan, kirtan, and gungaan are used as the vehicle: they generate the emotion that triggers the subconscious that lifts the veil.

The chain: Bina Hari kripa → no sant. Bina sant → no satsang. Bina satsang → no bhaav. Bina bhaav → no Bhagwan. (Without Hari's grace no saint is met; without a saint no satsang; without satsang no bhaav arises; without bhaav God is not found.) On need vs. love: most people call God out of need, and God knows it — "yet He still comes, for the bhaav. So even if the bhaav was born of need — daag achhe hain (these stains are good)." Need's mahima becomes love's garima. Without love no bhaav; without bhaav no Bhagwan. "Why does happiness arrive in the envelope of sorrow? That is Maya's veil."
8. Ashaeiynn HOUSEKEEPING NOTES (from this session)

Bhaiya urges everyone to watch all the Mool Tattva videos (30–40 videos, 1–1.5 hours each) — and to k eep doing jaap while watching, so that 50–100 hours of jaap accumulate alongside understanding. "Dekhna aapke upar hai — I for ce no one." Ashaeiynn deliberately keeps its membership small and selected: "Hamara motto drishti kholna hai" (our motto is to open your divya drishti). If crowds grow, attention scatters — Ashaeiynn works on drishti, unlike preachers whose visitors come only for blessings. "Because the day your drishti opens, you will see the mirror of the world." Everyone who reached Ashaeiynn has a purva-janma (past-life) connection being carried forward — "this bond is not of today ." "Samay bada balwan" — time is the mightiest; the right meeting happens only at the right time. Coming sessions will teach: the vidhi of attaining the Satguru (how to know Gurudev has accepted you).
9. QUICK RULES SUMMARY

1. Follow your traditions and social norms — never br eak the chain — but always KNOW the truth behind the ritual. 2. A one-day fast cannot buy a husband's lifespan or please Ganesh Bhagwan; continuous sadhna is what the original Mata did. Use festival days to grow love — that part is r eal. 3. Don't take celebrity preachers' socially-convenient statements at face value; test them against practice. Listen to discourses, but keep discernment. 4. First attain bhakti yourself; through it, uplift your parents. Appease Bhagwan, not people — kripa upstream ﬁx es relationships downstream. 5. No person is inherently bad — absence of Bhagwan's kripa-tarang mak es them so. 6. Know your Bhagwan: the shakti that stands with you, guides you, and for whom you work while it works for you. Everything else is drama.

7. The three-level alignment: your instinct-shakti (First God) → Satguru (Hanuman Ji Maharaj) → Param Tattva (Kul Devta ﬁrst, then Isht, up to R am). Align all three and you manifest eﬀortlessly . 8. A human guru gives bhakti and naam, never the full vidya. Multiple shaktis never come from one human body. The Satguru alone holds every vidya — including fr eeing you from pitrs. 9. Puja reaches the Kul Devta only after freedom from pitrs (only ~10% of pitrs are good) via the Guru's sharan. 10. You are an aspirant until Gurudev sits on your guru-sthaan — and he does not accept anyone cheaply. 11. Guard your "x = a": belief held till the end reveals truth; doubt in your own assumption collapses everything. 12. Never chase foundation-shaking knowledge (e.g., "how was the universe made") — gyaan without bhakti ﬁnds no Bhagwan. 13. Bhaav is the trigger: kirtan → emotion → subconscious → Maya's veil lifts. Even need-born bhaav is accepted by God.
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 3, English)
Who Is Your God? — Satguru, Param Tattva & the Power of Belief
User-style questions with answers grounded in Bhaiya's discourse. Greeting style: "Jai Siya Ram."

Q1. Does the Karwa Chauth fast really increase my husband's life? A: Jai Siya Ram! Bhaiya addressed this directly: the claim that a one-day fast increases the husband's lifespan is completely wrong (sarasar galat). What the fast genuinely does is increase love and aﬀection between husband and wife — the dr essing up, the gifts, the togetherness — and that is a beautiful thing worth doing. But remember: the Mata who began this vrat did not fast for one day; Ganesh Bhagwan is never pleased by a single day's fast. Real tapasya is continuous. So keep the tradition — never br eak your parampara — but know the truth behind it.

Q2. Should I stop following traditions then, since some beliefs behind them are wrong? A: No — never . Bhaiya is emphatic: never break your traditions, never go against society; society will not spare you if you do. Follow the norms, maintain the chain. The goal is not rebellion but awareness — "you should know that." Do everything you do, but with knowledge of what is real and what is social custom. That knowledge changes how you do everything afterward.

Q3. A famous saint says parents are greater than God and serving them is everything. Is that true? A: Bhaiya's answer: authentically (in principle) the statement is true, but practically it is not — and he pointed out the duplicacy of pr eachers who left their own parents for decades of tapasya while preaching this. Saints often speak this way to walk with society. The real teaching: ﬁrst awak en yourself through Bhagwan's bhakti — only then can you truly uplif t (taar) your parents. Only those parents' feet are fully worshipable which have been washed in Bhagwan's charanamrit; where that hasn't happened, a child's duty is to attain bhakti himself and through it perform his parents' uddhar. Even your parents' love for you ﬂows thr ough Bhagwan's kripa. So respect discourses, but don't surrender your discernment to smooth words.

Q4. My own family has turned against me. Why? A: Understand this deeply: no person is inherently bad. Without Bhagwan's kripa-tarang, a person becomes bad on their own. If Bhagwan's kripa is on you, your mother stays with you, your father's hand stays on your head, siblings remain yours from afar — and even strangers stand by you lik e brothers. If kripa is

absent, even your own become strangers. So the ﬁx is not endless appeasement of people — "Maa ko mat manao, Bhagwan ko manao." Appease Bhagwan; the relationships follow. And keep this hope: when kripa returns, the same people return.

Q5. My mother loves me immensely. Isn't that her kripa on me? A: A young man told Bhaiya the same — "if I cough at night my mother brings ginger to my mouth; her kripa on me is great." Bhaiya corrected him warmly: you got it wrong, brother. It is Bhagwan's kripa on you that you received such a mother. Kripa is always upstream of every good relationship. Thank the mother — but r ecognize whose gift she is.

Q6. Who is my God? I worship Krishna, Hanuman Ji, Bholenath, my Kul Devta — I'm confused. A: That confusion is exactly the problem — people spend half their lives not knowing who THEIR Bhagwan is, and if you ﬁnd out, half your pr oblems end. Gurudev's deﬁnition: Bhagwan is that shakti which stands with you in every situation, guides you, consoles you, works for you while you work for it. You do for it; it does for you — and the pr oof is simple: your works keep happening. That shakti is Bhagwan for you. Everything beyond this deﬁnition is drama.

Q7. What is this "instinct" or gut feeling people talk about? A: That is your First God — the ﬁrst ener gy of your atma tattva ("atma so paramatma"). Behind every human stands one shakti from birth that keeps you connected to praan urja. The world calls it instinct or gut feeling — "I just felt lik e it." That feeling is the ﬁrst step of the ener gy that pulls you. It is what brought you to Ashaeiynn, what makes you join the meeting, what tells you "sit for 5 more minutes of jaap" when your body protests. Try to work on your instinct — it is a shakti speaking.

Q8. Is instinct the same as kundalini shakti? A: No. Kundalini shakti must be awakened through dhyaan-yog — it does not operate by default. The shakti behind you (instinct) is pr esent and working from birth. Don't confuse the two.

Q9. What is the three-level alignment Bhaiya taught? A: Level 1 — your F irst God: the shakti behind you (instinct), which pulls you. Level 2 — the Satguru: the ener gy that joins your shakti to a divine energy; your Satguru is Shri Gurudev Shri Hanuman Ji Maharaj. Level 3 — the Param Tattva: the supreme element above all — our R am (called Shyam, Sitaram, Murari, Tripurari by diﬀer ent people), and Mahadev also belongs there — with your K ul Devta coming FIRST in the param order, then your Isht. Without a Satguru you cannot reach the Param Tattva, and without the Param Tattva you cannot manifest anything. The one who aligns all three needs nothing — he sits and manifests, and it happens.

Q10. Why does my puja to my Kul Devta bring no results? A: Because puja reaches the Kul Devta only when the path is clear. First you must get free of the pitrs and take the Guru's sharan — otherwise your puja never r eaches. Exception: if your pitrs are good, it passes through — but only about 10 out of 100 pitrs are good. And never treat your Kul Devta as "small deities of a small temple" — in the P aram Tattva order, the Kul Devta comes before even your Isht.

Q11. Can't I just take a human guru? Many great saints give diksha. A: You can — and you will receive bhakti, naam, and a mantra, which are real. If the parampara is true, its disciples do advance. But hear the guarantee: they never advance in gyaan-vigyaan-paravigyaan, because multiple kinds of shaktis can never come from one human body. A bhakti-parampara guru cannot teach pret-removal, because no one in his lineage ever knew it. If you make a human body your Satguru, you'll get nothing in the name of vidya. The Satguru — Hanuman Ji Maharaj — holds every gyaan you could need.

Q12. What happened with the man who had four gurus? A: A man with a medical shop chanted "Radhe Krishna" all day for years and had taken diksha from four gurus in Mathura. Bhaiya saw all four guru-paramparas standing in lines behind him with heaps of siddhis — and yet the man had no money to eat, and his pitrs sat crowned on a throne inside his body, feeding like kings on his mantra-energy. Not one guru or siddhi in those lineages knew how to remove them. One danda of Gurudev resolved it. Lesson: lineage-count and siddhi-count are not vidya. And remember — siddhis ar e loyal to no one; they abandon one person for another.

Q13. If I ask Hanuman Ji Maharaj to be my Guru, will he accept immediately? A: Ask a human and he'll say "OK" at once. Ask Hanuman Ji Maharaj and he will say "chal, hawa aane de" — not so fast! Because the Guru's dayitva is the gr eatest responsibility in this world, and Gurudev does not take anyone into his sharan cheaply. Until Gurudev sits upon your guru-sthaan, you are only an aspirant. The vidhi of attaining the Satguru — and how to know you've been accepted — is being taught in the coming Mool T attva sessions. Meanwhile: keep the jaap, keep the bhaav, watch the Mool Tattva videos to understand why you were pulled here at all.

Q14. What is the "Let x = a" teaching? A: Every math problem says "Find x," and we solve it by ﬁrst writing "L et x = a" — and by holding that assumption to the end, the TRUE value of x emerges. Faith works identically: by believing, the truth reveals itself — the one who believes, before him Bhagwan manifests, and it is true. But if you doubt your assumption mid-equation, everything collapses instantly. And if you keep switching assumptions on others' advice ("take x = 1!" "no, x = 2!"), your vishwas cracks and no result ever comes. Your whole spiritual shakti is built on your held "x = a." Guard it with your life.

Q15. Can you tell me how the universe was made? A: This question Bhaiya has permanently declined — and he tells the story of why . When he himself asked Gurudev, he stopped Gurudev mid-answer: "If I hear the rest, my faith in you will shake, and my foundation with it." Once, he taught just one-fourth of that knowledge in a session — and that very day attacks began on 90% of those present, because Gurudev stepped back one step; recovery took months. Some knowledge shakes your existence and costs more than it gives. So: never ask how the universe was made. Take gyaan freely — but only as much as your bhakti can car ry.

Q16. Which matters more — gyaan or bhakti? A: However much gyaan a person gathers, if the bhakti tattva is not in him, he will never ﬁnd Bhagwan. Bhaiya's wor ds: "Take as much gyaan from me as you want — ﬁll yourself . But as you leave, take bhakti with you." At the Mahotsav, Gurudev distributes bhakti with both hands — the whole year r emains for gyaan.

Q17. Why do bhajan and kirtan matter so much? A: Because of the bhaav cycle. The veil of Maya is removed through your subconscious mind, and the subconscious is triggered by emotion (bhaav). Bhajan-kirtan generate the bhaav that triggers the subconscious that lifts the veil — which is why one with pure bhaav has a direct connection. The chain runs: without Hari's kripa no sant; without a sant no satsang; without satsang no bhaav; without bhaav no Bhagwan.

Q18. I only remember God when I need something. Is my devotion fake? A: Bhagwan knows you are calling out of need — and He still comes, for the bhaav . Even if the bhaav was born of need, "daag achhe hain" — those stains ar e good. Need's mahima becomes love's garima over time. What matters is that bhaav arises at all; keep calling, and let the need ripen into love.

Q19. Healers oﬀer reiki / lama-fera to remove negative energy . Do they work? A: Bhaiya's caution from a real case: a 30-year-old came trembling, and Bhaiya saw the man's deceased father seated inside his body — move the pitru aside and the tr embling stopped. Worldly healers oﬀering "healing techniques" cannot even see who is sitting inside — "blind men setting out to cure others' pain." Removal of pitrs is a vidya that comes only from the Satguru. Don't hand yourself to those without drishti.

Q20. Why does Ashaeiynn stay so small? Why not spread like the famous ashrams? A: Deliberately. "Hamara motto drishti kholna hai" — Ashaeiynn's motto is opening your divya drishti, not gathering crowds for blessings. When crowds grow, attention scatters. Everyone who reached Ashaeiynn carries a past-life connection being carried forward — this bond is not of today . And "samay bada balwan" — the right meeting happens only at the right time.
